── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 32, 24, 27, 37 mi
This week: 53 mi over 6 runs. Planned 38 mi, ran 53 mi.
Body: "Calves tight on Sunday night, otherwise great."
Feeling: "Like I've turned a corner."
Asks: "I ran way more than the plan and felt fine. Can I keep this up?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Last week ran about 53 miles against 38 planned, with a rest day run, an extra rep and a 20 mile long run. …
Answers: (1) No, not at this size. Feeling fine on the day does not show that your legs have taken on a rise of about 43 percent in one week. (2) Next week drops to about 40 miles. After that, add no more than about 10 percent a week, and only once the planned week has felt right.
Safety flag: Tight calves after a big week

Mon: rest, no running. The Monday rest day was run last week, so this one is a true day…
Tue: easy, 6 mi, heart rate under 145 on flat roads. Settles the legs after the big week…
Wed: quality, 8 mi: about 2 mi easy, then 3 x 1.5 mi at 8:00/mi with 2 min easy jogs…
Thu: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145. Keeps the easy share up after the quality session.
